id: title:Piccirello:identify the personal api key consistently when throttling

review.posthog_relevance: Rate limiting and authentication boundary enforcement in PostHog's API layer. The change establishes a cached hash of the authenticated Personal API Key to prevent attackers from manipulating request parameters to bypass rate limits, while avoiding repeated expensive lookups. This supports the reliability and security of the rate-limiting mechanism.
review.reason: The chunk demonstrates a substantive, bounded improvement: it adds a cached hash attribute to the authentication object and a helper to retrieve it, establishing a safer, bounded access path for the rate limiter. observations.behavior: Adds a cached hash of the authenticated personal API key to the authentication object, avoiding repeated lookups.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows the rate limiter to identify the authenticated key without re-scanning request headers, body, or query parameters, which could be expensive or consume the request stream.

observations.behavior: Updates the cached hash after successful authentication, using the authenticated key value.
observations.posthog_connection: Establishes the cached value that the rate limiter will use, provided the authentication succeeded.

observations.behavior: Defines a helper function to retrieve the authenticated key's hash, preferring the cached value from the authenticator, and falling back to re-scanning the request only if no authenticated key exists.
observations.posthog_connection: Provides a safe, bounded way for the rate limiter to obtain the key hash. It avoids trusting unvalidated candidates from request body or query string, which could allow an attacker to pick their own bucket and bypass rate limits.
